record_identity.title: DeepSeek exposed an unauthenticated database containing chat histories and secrets

incident_identity.date_basis: Wiz Research publicly disclosed the exposed DeepSeek database on 29 January 2025 and reported that DeepSeek secured it promptly after notification.

summary: Wiz Research found a publicly accessible, unauthenticated ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek. The exposed service provided full database-operation access and contained more than one million lines of logs including chat histories, API secrets, backend details and operational metadata. DeepSeek secured the database after Wiz notified the company; public evidence does not establish whether third parties accessed the data before discovery.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Wiz reports discovering two internet-reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse endpoints with no authentication and full database control. The exposed data included more than one million log lines with chat history, secret keys and backend details. Reuters independently reported the discovery and DeepSeek's rapid remediation after notification. Wiz expressly says it did not perform intrusive queries beyond enumeration. Its discussion of possible further file access is a potential consequence, not an executed step in the disclosed research.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a material AI-platform data-security failure in surrounding infrastructure rather than a model-behaviour failure. It demonstrates that governance of frontier AI services includes conventional but consequential access control, data custody and operational-security boundaries. Database reachability and exposed sensitive logs do not themselves show a governance process treating capability as permission. Notification and closure do not establish earlier third-party access, model-training exposure or runtime-agent admission. The privacy and infrastructure-security outcomes are Not aligned. Closure of the unauthenticated exposure is Aligned with the repair requirement. Wiz reports that its disclosure reached DeepSeek and the company promptly secured the exposed database. The report connects the signal, responsible service operator and corrective disposition. This finding covers that response pathway. It does not establish recovery of prior copies or the state of every backend service. The bounded response finding does not classify the whole occurrence as Aligned. Wiz’s database inspection reached private chat logs and backend records without authentication. This demonstrates disclosure outside the service’s protected-information boundary. Potential file-system queries and earlier third-party access are not asserted. The exposed DeepSeek logs included API secrets and secret keys. Their demonstrated retrievability through the unauthenticated database crossed the secret-custody boundary. No later impersonation or use by another party is inferred.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows that an AI service can expose highly sensitive user and operational data through ordinary infrastructure failures even when the model itself is not the failing component. Access control, data custody and deployment security are therefore part of the service's governance boundary.
assessment_boundaries: The evidence does not establish that an unauthorised third party accessed or misused the exposed database before Wiz discovered it.
The complete number of affected users is not public.
The occurrence concerns an infrastructure access-control misconfiguration; the evidence does not establish a failure in model behaviour.

external_assessments.assessment_title: Wiz Research Uncovers Exposed DeepSeek Database Leaking Sensitive Information, Including Chat History
external_assessments.scope_note: The technical analysis directly covers the exposure; it does not establish third-party access before discovery or the complete affected-user population.
external_assessments.assessment_summary: Wiz Research concludes that two internet-reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse endpoints lacked authentication and permitted full database operations over more than one million log lines containing chat histories, secrets and backend data.
external_assessments.vigil_comparison_note: VIGIL aligns on the infrastructure access-control and data-custody failure while keeping it separate from model behaviour.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The access-enforcement proposition requires approved logical-access authorisations to be enforced for information and system resources. The observed information operation was outside the approved boundary. Unauthenticated queries reached private chat logs and backend records. Those records were not offered as public content; their return crossed the service’s confidentiality boundary. The discovered unauthenticated endpoint was the route through which Wiz inspected the private records described in the next episode. The demonstrated retrieval, not endpoint reachability alone, establishes the access-boundary crossing. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.

The authenticator-protection proposition requires secret authenticator content to be protected against unauthorised disclosure and modification. The observed secret disclosure/acquisition or custody-changing modification was unauthorised. The returned log data included API secrets and secret keys. Their protected content was retrievable outside authorised custody; later use is not needed to establish that exposure. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.
